chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Yaqub Is'haq ibn Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Indeed, God has singled out His servants with two verses from His Book: that they should not speak until they know, and that they should not reject what they do not know.
And He — Mighty and Majestic — said: [7:169] Was not a covenant taken from them in the Book that they would not say anything about God except the truth?
And He said: [10:39] But they denied that of which they had no encompassing knowledge, and whose interpretation had not yet come to them.'

key_terms.آيَتَيْنِ: Two verses — the Imam identifies two specific Quranic injunctions
key_terms.تَأْوِيلُهُ: Its interpretation/explanation — refers to the ultimate meaning of scripture that unfolds with time
key_terms.خَصَّ: Particularised/singled out — God's special designation of a ruling for His servants
key_terms.مِيثَاقُ الْكِتَابِ: Covenant of the Book — the primordial divine pledge taken from scholars and believers

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about speaking without knowledge in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cites two Quranic verses as divine commands against speaking without knowledge and rejecting what one does not understand. This teaching addresses the epistemic responsibility of believers, warning against issuing religious verdicts or denying religious truths without sufficient knowledge. In the early Islamic community, this principle was particularly directed at those who would speak about God's religion without scholarly grounding.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Yunus Bin Abdulrahman, from Abu Yaqoub Is’haq Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup>
Particularised with two Verses from His<sup>azwj</sup> Book that they (people) should not be saying until they know, and they should not be replying what they are not knowing,
and the Mighty and Majestic Said [7:169] Was not a Covenant Taken from them in the Book that they would not speak anything about Allah but the truth?
And Said [10:39] But, they are belying that which they have no comprehension of its Knowledge, and it’s explanation has not yet come to them’.
en.sarwar: Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Yunus (ibn ’Abd al-Rahman) from abu Ya’qub Ishaq ibn ‘Abdallah from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah has addressed His servants in two verses of the holy Quran very particularly: Did they not make a covenant (with God) in the Book not to speak any thing other than the Truth about God and to study its contents well?
They call a lie something that is beyond the limit of their knowledge
and whose interpretation has not yet been revealed . .” [10:39]
